title: Memories of the Slumbering Ones
next_chapter_hook: In the depths of that silver-white Mental Sea, countless slumbering consciousnesses flickered like stars—Chen Ji finally realized that each of them had once been a candidate for the "Tianji Record."

text.content:
Pain seared through his head as if it would split apart.

Chen Ji felt as though an invisible hammer was repeatedly striking his Mental Sea, each blow bringing tearing agony. That power dormant for a thousand years surged forth like a broken dam, carrying countless shattered images and sounds, flooding in with tremendous force.

He saw vast wilderness, saw countless cultivators kneeling in grand ceremonies, saw that gaze overlooking all living beings—cold, scrutinizing, like a deity examining ants.

These were not his memories.

So why were they so clear?

"Ji'er..."

A voice of utmost tenderness resonated in the depths of his consciousness, like a mother calling to a child returning from a distant journey. Chen Ji shuddered all over—it was Chen Tianming's voice! The voice of his father, long faded from memory!

Following the牵引 of that voice, Chen Ji's consciousness was dragged deeper into the Mental Sea. There was a faint light, and within it, the silhouette of a middle-aged man was barely visible. He stood with his back to all living beings, facing an invisible barrier, his shoulders bearing something extremely heavy.

"Find her... protect her..."

The voice came in fragments, like a candle flame in the wind,随时都会熄灭.

The scene abruptly shifted.

Chen Ji saw a majestic altar, and suspended in its center was a yellowed bamboo slip—that slip emanated exactly the same aura as the Tianji Record in his bloodline.

No, not just one.

Beneath that altar, dozens of seals were neatly arranged, each containing a sleeping figure. Their faces varied from old to young, but each had a golden mark on their Brow Center—identical to Chen Ji's.

That was the brand of the Tianji Record.

And that brand was slowly dissipating—with each one that faded, the bamboo slip on the altar grew brighter.

dialogue.content:
"Candidates will ultimately become nourishment."

That voice was ice-cold and thorough, filled with undeniable authority.

"Only the final victor is worthy of inheriting all the secrets of the Tianji Record. As for the others... they are merely fuel."

text.content:
Chen Ji's blood seemed to freeze.

He finally understood! Those missing geniuses, those bizarre breaks in inheritance, those inexplicably fallen powerhouses—they did not die by accident or enemy hands, but were used as fuel by this so-called "Heavenly Dao" and sacrificed to the Tianji Record!

And he himself, from the very beginning, was part of this sacrifice.

Those fragments he deemed as opportunities, those foresight abilities he took pride in—nothing more than fodder scattered to livestock being fattened by the Heavenly Dao!

Fierce fury churned in the Mental Sea, but immediately, an even more terrifying thought emerged—

What about Chen Nian?

That sister taken away by the Holy Sect, that girl called the "Heavenly Fate Lock Key"... was she also caught in this sacrifice?

Her safety, her fate, the truth behind her disappearance—everything seemed to point in the same direction.

That altar.

Those seals.

Chen Ji felt his Heavenly Fate Value draining at an unprecedented rate.

choice.prompt: Facing this cruel truth and the torrent of memory fragments flooding in, Chen Ji had to make a choice—

choices.description: Surrender to the river of memories, allow those images that don't belong to him to overwhelm him, attempting to piece together more truths from the fragments.
choices.risk_hint: Consciousness may be corroded by ancient will

text.content:
Chen Ji abandoned resistance and let the river of memories overwhelm him.

More images flooded into his Mental Sea—he saw the catastrophe of ten thousand years ago, countless cultivators turning to ash, the cold gaze of the Heavenly Dao's Eye.

He also saw a person.

That person stood atop the altar, back to all living beings, with a golden mark on their Brow Center identical to Chen Ji's—the previous generation's Tianji Record inheritor, also Chen Ji's ancestor.

"Someday," that person suddenly turned, their gaze seeming to穿越时空 and stare directly at Chen Ji, "someone will break this cycle."

choices.description: Forcefully sever the connection to memories, reject accepting this cruel truth, guard your consciousness boundaries.
choices.process_label: 用意志力斩断记忆锁链

text.content:
Chen Ji gritted his teeth,凝聚 all his consciousness into a barrier.

"Get out!"

He roared in his heart, forcefully severing the connection to those memory fragments. Violent backlash left him with splitting headaches and faint blood seeping from his seven orifices, but his consciousness finally regained control of his Mental Sea.

The cost was severe—those precious memory fragments slipped through his fingers like sand, never to be reclaimed.

But Chen Ji did not regret.

He would rather be an ignorant piece than become nourishment on someone else's chessboard!

choices.description: Use one's own will as the guiding force, actively absorb and refine these memory fragments, grasp fate in your own hands.
choices.visible_reward: Gains partial ancestral memories and abilities
choices.risk_hint: Success rate extremely low, failure results in complete annihilation

text.content:
A flash of determination crossed Chen Ji's eyes.

Since becoming a piece is inevitable, then I shall be the one who plays the game!

He no longer resisted, nor did he indulge. Instead, he used his own will as a furnace, refining those memory fragments one by one.

Agonizing pain struck, Chen Ji felt as though his soul was being roasted over flames. But with each fragment refined, he gained a measure of strength, knowledge, and insight into fate.

When the final fragment was absorbed, Chen Ji slowly opened his eyes.

In the depths of his pupils, there was now a touch of vicissitudes and profundity—the gaze only an ancient monster who had lived for ten thousand years would possess.

The river of memories receded, and Chen Ji finally regained control of his body.

He found himself still standing in place, as if everything just now was merely a momentary illusion. But the faintly burning golden mark on his Brow Center, and those fragmented images now residing in his Mental Sea, reminded him—it was not an illusion.

He had seen too much.

The sacrifices of ten thousand years ago, the falls of inheritors through the ages, the布局 of the Heavenly Dao's Eye... and, an astonishing fact—

Those slumbering ones within the seals were not all dead.

Chen Ji closed his eyes and probed deep into his Mental Sea with his divine sense.

There, he saw a silver-white sea of stars. Countless stars flickered in the sea—some bright as the scorching sun, candidates not yet sacrificed; some dim like dying embers, fuel about to be exhausted.

And he himself was merely an insignificant star in this sea.

But now, he knew.

He knew he was not alone, knew that among those slumbering stars, perhaps some shared his goal—to break this cycle, to destroy this sacrifice.

And Chen Nian... perhaps imprisoned somewhere in a corner of the altar, waiting to be rescued.

"Found it..."

Chen Ji murmured softly, the corners of his lips lifting slightly.

Though the cost was severe—his Heavenly Fate had been consumed by nearly a third—he gained something far more precious than what was lost:

The truth.

And, a direction.

He was no longer a headless fly bumping around as a piece, but a player holding the chess manual. He knew the weakness of the Heavenly Dao's Eye, knew the altar's location, knew of the slumbering ones' existence.

Now, all he needed was a map, a plan, and sufficient strength.

Just as Chen Ji was organizing his thoughts, a faint fluctuation suddenly came from deep within his Mental Sea.

He followed that波动, only to see a star in the depths of the star sea trembling violently. That star emanated a faint yet familiar aura—that was Chen Nian's aura!

"Brother... brother..."

Intermittent cries echoed in the Mental Sea, like a drowning person's plea. Chen Ji's heart clenched—Chen Nian was alive! She was struggling within that seal, sending him a rescue signal!

But that seal was so powerful, with Chen Ji's current strength, he simply could not reach it.

"Wait for me."

Chen Ji said silently in his heart, "I will come save you."

Ye Qing's figure suddenly appeared beside Chen Ji.

"You just now..." she frowned, concern filling her gaze, "your aura was in such chaos, I thought you'd gone into走火入魔."

Chen Ji smiled faintly, that smile carrying a touch of post-crisis relief: "I just saw some... things I shouldn't have seen."

He did not hide it.

Since he'd decided to cooperate with Ye Qing, some truths had to be let known. Moreover, those memory fragments also revealed one thing—the Demonic Path Holy Sect was precisely one of the Heavenly Dao's Eye's representatives in the mortal world.

Ye Qing's situation was far more dangerous than she imagined.

"I need to tell you something."

Chen Ji's voice was low and serious, "Regarding your sect, the Heavenly Dao, and... our true enemy."

Ye Qing's expression gradually grew grave.

When Chen Ji described those images from the memory fragments one by one, Ye Qing's face turned ashen. She finally understood why the elders of the Holy Sect always looked at her with those tool-like gazes.

From the very beginning, she was a selected piece.

And now, Chen Ji gave her another choice—break this chessboard, free all the pieces.

"I'm in." Ye Qing毫不犹豫 said, flames of revenge burning in her eyes, "Tell me what to do."

Chen Ji nodded, his gaze cast toward the distant horizon.

He knew he had embarked on a road of no return. From this moment, he was no longer just a废物 disciple, a player pretending to be weak to devour the strong—he was a rebel challenging the Heavenly Dao's will, the first among the candidates destined to be sacrificed to awaken a rebellious consciousness.

The road ahead was long, full of thorns.

The terror of the Heavenly Dao's Eye was far beyond what his current strength could contend with. Among those slumbering stars, who knew how many had long been ground down in will, becoming fuel-like walking corpses.

But Chen Ji would not retreat.

Because what he saw was not just despair, but hope—that star struggling and crying for help in the depths of the sea, that girl sealed in a corner of the altar.

That was his sister, also his only weakness.

For her sake, even if it meant opposing Heaven, what fear?

Just as Chen Ji made his decision, ripples再次泛起 in the star sea within his Mental Sea.

That一直沉睡的 star suddenly lit up, emanating an aura almost identical to Chen Ji's. Then, a voice, ancient and feeble, rang in his mind:

"Successor... you have finally come..."

Chen Ji shuddered all over.

That voice... that was the voice of Mo Xiansheng, the guardian of the first page of the Tianji Record! But why was it coming from deep within the star sea?

Could it be that Mo Xiansheng... was also one of those slumbering ones?

No, perhaps more accurately—Mo Xiansheng was precisely the only one among those slumbering ones to successfully break free from the seal and retain sanity!

Chen Ji finally understood why Mo Xiansheng always只 said half the truth—because that's all he truly could say.

"Do you think you are the only one selected?"

That voice continued, carrying endless vicissitudes and desolation.

"The candidates for the Tianji Record were never just one. Through ten thousand years, how many like you awakened the ability to foresee the future, how many struggled repeatedly between hope and despair, ultimately turning to fuel on the altar..."

Chen Ji沉默着, listening to this narration from antiquity.

"You are the first to choose resistance after awakening." A touch of gratification appeared in that voice, "But remember, the Heavenly Dao's Eye is far more terrifying than you imagine. It is not one person, but a collective will accumulated across countless ages."

"Behind you, countless eyes are watching your every move."

"Do not underestimate, do not reveal your true purpose."

"Before the time comes, you are still that废物 disciple—this must not change."

The voice gradually faded, and the star sea returned to calm.

Chen Ji slowly opened his eyes to find Ye Qing staring at him nervously.

"Are you... okay?" she asked carefully.

Chen Ji nodded, reapplying that harmless smile to his face: "It's nothing, just thought of some... interesting things."

Interesting things?

If Ye Qing knew what惊涛骇浪 he had just experienced, what a massive chess game he had glimpsed, she probably wouldn't be smiling.

But this was precisely what Chen Ji needed.

Under the gaze of the Heavenly Dao's Eye, he had to act as usual—a废物 disciple fatefully toyed with, a menial servant只知道苟且偷生.

Only this way could he lay low, accumulate strength, and wait for that moment that would determine his fate—all without drawing attention.

In the distant horizon, dark clouds were gathering.

Chen Ji looked up to see a tremendous eye slowly opening within those clouds. That eye was cold and majestic, overlooking the vast land, as if all things in the world were merely ants in its view.

The Heavenly Dao's Eye.

It was watching everything on this land, including Chen Ji standing here at this moment.

Chen Ji faced that gaze, a barely perceptible smile curling his lips.

"Watching me?" he silently said in his heart, "Then watch carefully
